newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA CALL ENDS IN RANGE-BOUND TRADE, GILTS STEADY.
newsitem.headline: INDIA CALL ENDS IN RANGE-BOUND TRADE, GILTS STEADY.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday at 4.5 percent in quiet, range-bound trade ahead of an extended weekend, dealers said.
Banks in India's commercial capital of Bombay will be closed on Saturday for a local holiday.
Dealers said most of the day's trade was between 4.5 and 5.0 percent after opening at 4.0-5.0 percent.
Call money rates are exepected to move up next week after a 30-billion-rupee bond auction on Monday.
"Rates may not move up much as liquidity is still good," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "I do not see rates going up much...maybe 6.0 percent or so."
"Further it is not clear whether the repo auctions will continue through the month," he said. "In that case all those funds will come back to the system."
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has been conducting repo auctions regularly since February.
But this month, it has announced auction dates only for the first half of August, leading money market players to speculate whether the auctions will continue.
Dealers said prices of government securities were largely steady in quiet trade, with market players cautious ahead of Monday's bond auction.
Among actively-traded stocks, the 12.59 percent 2004 stock traded at 106.29 rupees against Thursday's close of 106.25.
The 12.50 percent 2004 was steady at 106.05 rupees, while 11.83 percent 2003 fell to 103.05 rupees, against its previous close of 103.15 rupees, dealers said.
The 12.14 percent 2000 stock saw deals in the region of 104.28 and 104.32 rupees, against the previous close of 104.36 rupees, dealers said.
